title: Platform sync: routing + quotas digest (Apr 18 2026)
body:
Platform weekly sync — control plane / routing / auth / quotas
Date: 2026-04-18
Time: 10:30–11:00 PT
Location: #platform-eng weekly call (Zoom link in Slack)
Attendees: Avery Chen (owner), Diego Morales, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor, Sara Kim, Jonah (SRE), external: none

Agenda:
- Quick metrics snapshot (Avery)
- Control plane: API health, rollout status, hotfixes (Diego)
- Routing and policy layer: fallback rules, region routing, cost-tiering (Priya)
- Auth & quotas: token throttles, quota enforcement edge cases (Liam)
- Blockers / escalations / action items

Notes / discussion:
1) Metrics snapshot
- Control plane API: 99p latency for write endpoints is ~122ms (last week 98ms) — spike coincides with Canary config change on Apr 16.
- Error rate: overall 0.14% 5xx across control plane; spike to 0.6% on Apr 16 03:00 UTC (investigation below).
- Quotas: 12 customers at 90% of quota in the last 48h (mostly embedding-heavy workloads).
- Routing decisions: region fallback triggered 18 times for us-west on Apr 15 during the EC2 AZ maintenance window; automatic fallback to us-east worked as designed but increased p99 by ~40ms for those requests.

2) Control plane health & rollouts (Diego)
- Canary rollout for controller v1.4.2 completed to 20% traffic; we saw connection churn with the new retry backoff algorithm leading to brief 5xxs (Jira PLAT-4823). Diego: rolled back the backoff changes and redeployed; monitoring shows error rate normalized.
- Hotfix applied: PR #512 reverted the backoff tweak. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/512.
- Next steps: rework retry backoff to be connection-aware (idea: track per-connection failures, increase window slowly). Diego + Jonah pairing Wed Apr 21.

3) Routing & policy layer (Priya)
- Cost-tiering policy tests: ran traffic simulation against tiered routing table, results show expected cost savings but route churn under bursty traffic.
- Observed issue: prefix-based routing rules don't respect per-account burst overrides when cache TTL is very short — leads to flapping between primary/secondary routes. Filed PLAT-4899.
- Short-term mitigation: increase route cache TTL for affected accounts to 30s and add jitter on route recompute. Priya to land patch by Apr 20.
- Long-term: design doc in Confluence: Platform-Routing-Design-v2. Action: schedule design review with solutions-eng and SRE next Tues Apr 22.

4) Auth & quotas (Liam)
- Quota enforcement: found two edge cases where incremental quota grants during token refresh were double-counted, causing unexpected transient rejections for streaming sessions. Root cause: race between token-refresh hook and per-request counter increment.
- Fix: atomic increment change landed in service-auth v0.9.1; tests pass, rolling to staging today. Liam to monitor for 48h.
- Token throttles: adding a small token-bucket allowance for 'long-poll' websocket sessions to avoid timeouts; experiment flagged as draft in repo.

5) Incident post-mortem draft review (brief)
- Apr 16 incident (5xx spike) — preliminary notes: related to the canary config + route recompute TTL. Diego to draft post-mortem and link to PLAT-4823. Target publish Apr 21.

6) Blockers / escalations
- Blocker: some enterprise customers approaching quotas; account team needs temporary quota increases while we tune batching/Optimize suggestions. Action: Priya to prepare list and recommended temporary increases by EOD Apr 19.
- Blocker: flaky e2e test for routing policies failing in CI; causes delay in merging fixes. Liam + Sara to pair and stabilize tests, target Apr 23.

Action items (owner — due)
- Diego: pair with Jonah to design connection-aware retry backoff; prototype by Apr 25.
- Priya: increase route cache TTL for flagged accounts and land jitter mitigation; PR by Apr 20.
- Liam: monitor auth fix in staging; report by Apr 20 (48h watch).
- Avery: coordinate with GTM for customer quota bumps for at-risk customers; list to Priya by Apr 19.
- Sara + Liam: stabilize routing policy e2e tests; aim to merge by Apr 23.
- Diego: publish incident post-mortem for Apr 16 spike; target Apr 21.

Decisions made:
- Rollback backoff change immediately when connection churn observed; rework offline.
- Increase default route cache TTL from 5s -> 10s globally as a temporary safety net.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Evaluate whether route recompute should be debounced per-account with exponential backoff.
- Look into making per-account route preferences sticky for short durations to reduce flapping.
- Consider exposing a customer-facing advisory if we plan quota throttling changes.

Follow-ups & next meeting:
- Next sync: 2026-04-25 10:30 PT
- Pre-work: Priya to publish routing test results; Liam to publish staging auth metrics.

Quick reference links referenced in this doc:
- Jira: PLAT-4823 (canary backoff spike), PLAT-4899 (routing cache flapping)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/512
- Confluence: Platform-Routing-Design-v2

Raw slack threads / context: #platform-alerts Apr 16 spike, #platform-routing for TTL discussion.

Status summary sentence for exec update: control plane remains healthy after rollback; routing TTL and auth race fixes are highest priority — expect reduced p99 and fewer quota surprises by end of next week if patches land on schedule.

End of notes.
